safety.inFlightStopBehavior: No new request or run starts after stop; because the official SDK exposes no physical AbortSignal, the run remains occupied until the in-flight transport settles.
residualRisks: The official Firecrawl SDK transport cannot be physically cancelled mid-request, so a stop may wait for that single in-flight request and may still consume its credit.
Image hosts are resolved and required to be public before every request and redirect, but DNS lookup and fetch are separate operations; DNS rebinding remains a local-MVP TOCTOU risk.
Small run event arrays are atomically rewritten per event; this remains suitable for the bounded personal target but is not a database or distributed queue.
